page: Amazon Web Services m8a.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores operating at up to 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core ratio. The memory subsystem consists of 192 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, allocating exactly 4 GB of RAM per core. The instance lacks integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and delivers a baseline network throughput of 22 Gbps.

Hardware vector processing and cryptographic operations are accelerated via support for AVX-512 extensions, including AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and VAES. In computational benchmarks, the platform demonstrates top-tier results in both single-core and multi-core evaluations, registering a multi-core score of 29,981 in Geekbench and 102,059 in PassMark CPU suites. Memory bandwidth benchmarks reflect strong uncached read speeds of 290.37 GB/sec alongside uncached write speeds of 178.08 GB/sec.

With its 1:4 core-to-memory ratio and absence of bundled local disks, the system is designed to provide cost-efficient scalability for balanced CPU-to-memory resource footprints. The absence of on-board NVMe drives presents an operational tradeoff, requiring attached remote block volumes for persistence. The instance suits demanding multi-threaded workloads, including high-concurrency Redis caching instances, large software compilation pipelines, enterprise database hosting, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.12xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System and AMD EPYC 9R45 hardware. It features 48 dedicated physical x86_64 cores clocked at 4.5 GHz, paired with 192 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built-in instruction sets include AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16 extensions, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage, instead utilizing external network storage, and offers a baseline network speed of 22 Gbps. Across synthetic and practical benchmarks, m8a.12xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute capability, high uncached memory throughput, and strong performance in in-memory key-value operations such as Redis. This configuration is optimized for distributed databases, multi-threaded enterprise application backends, container orchestration, static web servers, and mid-range language model CPU inference pipelines.
